$comment: Coverage calendar seed. Every entry was mined from a live CREN article body or a committed brief in briefs/.
Nothing here was invented, inferred, or sharpened. Where a source gives only a month, date_precision is 'month'
and the date is recorded on the first of that month; where two CREN records disagree, confidence is 'unconfirmed'
and the disagreement is stated in the note. See frontend/docs/COVERAGE_CALENDAR.md.
Seeded 2026-09-04. Adding an entry: cite source_article_id or source_brief, and the source_url that establishes the date.

entries.headline: Franklin County Auditor's informal 2026 value review window closes
entries.summary: The free informal review is the simplest way a Franklin County owner can challenge the 2026 triennial value before the formal Board of Revision route opens.
entries.source_label: Franklin County Auditor, via CREN briefs
entries.note: CREN's own records disagree. briefs/2026-08-09-seo-report.md says the review window 'closes Sept 5, 2026'; briefs/2026-08-18.md and briefs/2026-08-09-social-listener.md say informal review sessions run 'July through September 2026'. Held as unconfirmed: confirm with the Auditor before publishing a date.

entries.headline: Ohio Brownfield Remediation Program's $120M round closes to applications
entries.summary: Applications for the round that opened Aug. 11 are accepted through Sept. 11 at development.ohio.gov. Franklin County applicants coordinate through COCIC.
entries.source_label: Ohio Department of Development program page, cited in CREN's Aug. 11 story
entries.note: briefs/2026-08-11.md records the window as 10 a.m. Aug. 11 to 5 p.m. Sept. 11, attributed to WCSM Radio and GrantedAI. CREN has already covered the opening; a closing-day piece has to add something the opening story did not.

entries.headline: Columbus Oktoberfest runs Sept. 11-13 at the Ohio Expo Center
entries.summary: Free admission, paid parking, three days at the Ohio Expo Center and State Fairgrounds. German Village roots are documented; the festival is not evidence of housing demand.
entries.note: CREN already published on this festival on July 8, 2026 — nine weeks before the search spike. Any fresh piece must be a genuinely different story and clear the publish gate's duplicate guard on its own terms.

entries.headline: Downtown Commission takes up the Diocese's demolition application for 197 E. Gay St.
entries.summary: The Roman Catholic Diocese of Columbus filed a Certificate of Appropriateness to demolish its 1908 five-story building and convert the site to surface parking. The Commission must approve demolition in the historic district.
entries.note: CREN's Sept. 3 story states the Commission agenda had not been formally published as of writing. Confirm the agenda on columbus.gov before drafting, and report the result, not the schedule.

entries.headline: Final approval hearing in the $359.9M RealPage rent-pricing settlement
entries.summary: Six landlord operators named in the DOJ suit manage central Ohio apartments, so the settlement's calendar reaches Columbus renters directly.
entries.source_label: TopClassActions.com, quoted in the Aug. 10 social-listener brief
entries.note: The brief quotes the date but records no exact URL, only the outlet name. Find the court's own docket or the settlement administrator's page before using this date in print.

entries.headline: Zone In Phase 2 public comment period closes
entries.summary: The 60-day comment window on the Phase 2 draft — nine new districts across roughly 40 percent of the city's parcels — opened Aug. 25 and closes Oct. 24 at columbus.gov/zoningupdate.
entries.source_label: City of Columbus zoning update page
entries.note: CREN covered the draft release and the opening of the window on Aug. 23. The closing-day story is a different piece: what was submitted, by whom, and what Council does next.

entries.headline: Columbus 'Our Voice Our Choice' participatory budget opens to public voting
entries.summary: City Council set aside $1M per district ($9M total) for capital improvements chosen by residents. Proposals closed Aug. 28; the city reviewed them through September and October.
entries.note: The brief records voting as opening 'November 2 onward'. Treat Nov. 2 as the start of a window, not a one-day event, and confirm the schedule on common.oneproject.org/en/columbus before drafting.

entries.headline: Upper Arlington votes on a $273.5M school bond and 4.9-mill operating levy
entries.summary: The final ballot package is a $273.5 million bond plus a separate 4.9-mill operating levy; the estimated bond increase is 2.25 mills above current collections.
entries.source_label: Upper Arlington Schools, June 30 board resolution summary
entries.note: CREN's existing piece is a correction of an earlier headline, not election coverage. The tax-impact-per-home angle for Upper Arlington owners is unwritten.

entries.headline: Dublin's Christkindlmarkt opens at Riverside Crossing Park
entries.summary: The free, German-inspired holiday market runs Nov. 21 through Dec. 24, 2026 at the base of the Dublin Link, under an operating agreement Dublin City Council approved in November 2025.
entries.source_label: City of Dublin news release, Aug. 28, 2026
entries.note: Market runs through Dec. 24, 2026. CREN's Aug. 28 announcement story left the chalet count and vendor list unconfirmed — an opening-week piece can close those gaps.

entries.headline: Deadline for renters to file a claim in the RealPage rent-pricing settlement
entries.summary: Eligibility turns on whether a renter's landlord used RealPage software, not on the renter. Ohio is a named affected state and claims are free to file.
entries.source_label: classaction.org / TopClassActions.com, quoted in the Aug. 9 and Aug. 10 social-listener briefs
entries.note: Two CREN briefs quote this date from secondary outlets without recording an exact URL. Verify against the settlement administrator before publishing.

entries.headline: Franklin County Board of Revision complaint deadline for 2026 triennial values
entries.summary: The formal route to challenge a 2026 triennial value after the informal review window closes. The 2026 update averaged a 9 percent residential increase and affects 2027 tax bills.
entries.source_label: Franklin County Auditor, cited in the Aug. 18 brief
entries.note: CREN has adjacent coverage from July 30, 2026 on challenging a reassessment. Confirm the deadline on the Auditor's Board of Revision page before drafting.

entries.headline: Kilbourne Run Sports Park Field 2 free walk-up window ends
entries.summary: Field 2 is open for walk-up play daily from noon to 9 p.m. from Aug. 1, 2026 through May 31, 2027, per the park's official page — the concrete answer to what the fee reversal actually bought.
entries.source_label: Columbus Recreation and Parks official park page
entries.note: A schedule end, not an announcement. Worth a story only if the city publishes what replaces the window.

entries.headline: Devon Triangle Phase 2 construction start (three remaining triplexes)
entries.summary: Habitat-MidOhio's first multifamily Columbus build. Phase 1 broke ground April 23 and started construction in May 2026; Phase 2 was described as beginning in September, with first families moving in by January 2027.
entries.note: A standing Monitoring Item across the Aug. 24-27 briefs. No primary source has confirmed a day. The trigger is habitatmidohio.org confirming a Phase 2 start date.

entries.headline: Ohio Stater at 1060 N. High St. scheduled to close for RPM Living's redevelopment
entries.summary: RPM Living proposed a seven-story, 270-unit mixed-use building with 865 beds on the Ohio Stater site. The existing 124-unit building was reported as closing in October 2026, displacing current tenants.
entries.note: Carried as a monitor in briefs/2026-05-07.md and briefs/2026-05-31.md, which name the UIDRB ruling and the closure as the two news hooks. Month only; no closing day published.

entries.headline: 'The Hanger' groundbreaking target on the former DeMonye's Greenhouse site
entries.summary: Rocky Point Partners bought the 5.73-acre property; developer Tom O'Brien confirmed a November 2026 groundbreaking target for 130 units at roughly $31 million, with residents expected in early 2028.
entries.note: A developer's stated target, not a scheduled event. Month only.

entries.headline: State Library of Ohio's lease at 274 E. First Ave. expires
entries.summary: The timeline anchor under Merus's proposal for five apartment buildings on the 7-acre Italian Village site: the site does not become fully available until the lease ends.
entries.source_label: NBC4, cited in the May 21 brief
entries.note: briefs/2026-08-24-social-listener.md records the same lease expiry and notes the Italian Village Commission has no hearing date yet — the hearing, not the lease date, is the likelier peg.
